concepts.name: Side effects
concepts.summary: Recognise actions such as mutating variables, printing, or writing files as side effects that make code less predictable.

concepts.name: Pure functions
concepts.summary: Explain that a pure function always returns the same output for the same input and changes nothing outside itself.

concepts.name: Immutable data
concepts.summary: Understand that values are not modified in place and that updates produce new values instead.

concepts.name: Functions as values
concepts.summary: Understand that functions can be stored in variables, passed as arguments, and returned like any other value.

concepts.name: Expressions versus statements
concepts.summary: Distinguish expressions that produce values from statements that perform actions, and see why functional style favours expressions.

concepts.name: Anonymous functions
concepts.summary: Recognise the syntax of an unnamed function written inline and know when it is used.

misconceptions.text: A function that prints output is still pure as long as it returns the right value.
Immutable data means a variable name can never be used again.
Functional programming simply means using functions, which every language already does.

concepts.name: Higher-order functions
concepts.summary: Write and use functions that accept or return other functions to parameterise behaviour.

concepts.name: Map, filter and reduce
concepts.summary: Apply map, filter and reduce to transform, select and aggregate collections without explicit loops.

concepts.name: Closures
concepts.summary: Use a function that remembers variables from the scope where it was defined, for example to build configurable functions.

concepts.name: Function composition
concepts.summary: Combine small functions so the output of one feeds the input of the next to build larger behaviour.

concepts.name: Recursion over data
concepts.summary: Replace loops with recursive functions that have a base case and a recursive case on lists or trees.

concepts.name: Copy-on-update techniques
concepts.summary: Update lists, maps and records by creating modified copies using spread, concat or similar operations.

misconceptions.text: Map and filter modify the original collection in place.
Reduce is only for summing numbers.
A closure copies the values of the captured variables at creation time.

concepts.name: Currying and partial application
concepts.summary: Transform multi-argument functions into chains of single-argument functions and fix some arguments to derive specialised functions.

concepts.name: Point-free pipelines
concepts.summary: Analyse and build data-transformation pipelines, judging when omitting explicit arguments helps or hurts readability.

concepts.name: Tail recursion and stack use
concepts.summary: Analyse when recursion grows the call stack and rewrite it with an accumulator in tail position.

concepts.name: Persistent data structures
concepts.summary: Explain how immutable collections share structure between versions to make updates efficient.

concepts.name: Explicit error handling types
concepts.summary: Represent absence and failure as values such as Option or Result rather than exceptions or nulls.

concepts.name: Functional core, imperative shell
concepts.summary: Analyse a program and restructure it so pure decision logic sits in a core and I/O sits in a thin outer layer, improving testability.

concepts.name: Lazy evaluation and iterators
concepts.summary: Use deferred computation to process large or infinite sequences and know when evaluation actually occurs.

misconceptions.text: Currying and partial application are the same thing.
Immutable collections must be fully copied on every update, so they are always slow.
Point-free style is always more readable than naming arguments.

concepts.name: Functors and mappable containers
concepts.summary: Analyse types that support mapping a function over their contents while preserving structure, and check the functor laws.

concepts.name: Monads for sequencing
concepts.summary: Use flatMap or bind to chain computations that may fail or carry context, and explain how they flatten nested containers.

concepts.name: Applicative validation
concepts.summary: Combine independent effectful values, for example accumulating all validation errors rather than stopping at the first.

concepts.name: Referential transparency and equational reasoning
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether an expression can be replaced by its value and use this to justify refactors and optimisations.

concepts.name: Algebraic data types
concepts.summary: Model domains with sum and product types so illegal states are unrepresentable, and consume them with pattern matching.

concepts.name: Effect modelling with IO
concepts.summary: Evaluate approaches that represent side effects as values that are described first and run at the program boundary.

concepts.name: Property-based testing
concepts.summary: Judge and write properties that should hold for all inputs, using generated data to test pure functions.

misconceptions.text: A monad is just a container or a way to perform side effects.
Property-based tests replace all example-based tests.
Pure functional code cannot perform I/O at all.

concepts.name: Paradigm trade-off evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate where functional techniques help or hurt in a given system considering performance, team skill, and domain.

concepts.name: Free monads and interpreters
concepts.summary: Design programs as data or abstract algebras that separate description from multiple interpreters.

concepts.name: Monad transformers and effect stacks
concepts.summary: Evaluate ways of combining several effects, such as state, errors and reader, against alternatives like effect handlers.

concepts.name: Optics for immutable updates
concepts.summary: Design composable accessors that read and update deeply nested immutable structures.

concepts.name: Type-level domain design
concepts.summary: Create type designs that encode invariants so the compiler rejects invalid programs.

concepts.name: Functional architecture patterns
concepts.summary: Design systems whose state is a fold over events or streams, with side effects pushed to the boundary.

concepts.name: Performance and memory analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate allocation, laziness-induced space leaks and fusion in functional code and decide on optimisations.

misconceptions.text: Functional code is always slower than imperative code because of immutability.
Stacking monad transformers is always the best way to combine effects.
A stronger type system removes the need for runtime validation and testing.
